We will run kurtosis now (geth, nethermind) to confirm it EthereumJS is passing pyspec and we do not have the logic in that commit fyi felix brought up a good point about the forkid issues we've had: https://ethereum-magicians.org/t/eip-6122-forkid-checks-based-on-timestamps/12130/2?u=matt i think our proposal is to update the EIP so that all active forks are written into the forkid e.g. this: https://github.com/ethereum/EIPs/pull/7487 well, we forked with geth on Kurtosis, so we will have to investigate it more on our side I agree with Felix' comment but the current state of your PR will not distinguish, since: > If multiple forks are applied at the same block or time, the block number or timestamp is checksummed only once. What we want is (right?): For shanghai: `<genesis hash> <homestead block (0)> <tangerine whistle (0> ... <shanghai time (0)>` For cancun: `<genesis hash> <homestead block (0)> <tangerine whistle (0> ... <shanghai time (0)> <cancun time (0)>` (all are padded to 4 bytes except ofc. genesis hash of 32 bytes). With the rule which I think it should be deleted, this is the result: For shanghai: `<genesis hash> <homestead block (0)>` For cancun: `<genesis hash> <homestead block (0)>` (i.e. still same CRC32) ah yes you are correct 👍 Is Constantinople + Petersburg considered one or two forks? Because if it is two forks per spec we get a problem if we remove that rule 🤔 (mainnet fork hashes will change) ~~i think one~~ looks like it is two also this only applies to timebased forks Ok but that should then be stated, because current EIP seems to read that it also applies to block nums I think it are two, will check in JS Ah right ofc the fork hashes are the same 😂 We should state it in the EIP though that there is an exception for Constantinople / Petersburg otherwise non-devnet forkhashes will change hmm originally i thought 2124 dealt differently with this but i realize now 6122 is basically the exact same just adding the notion of timestamp forking. i ask felix for clarification, but even before 6122 it was possible for the same genesis block to produce the same forkid for different fork configurations i asked felix for his thoughts, maybe best to not make any changes here sorry if my PR to the EIP was premature 😄 Not a problem I was about to approve it until I realized that it might not work as intended 🙂 I do agree that for same genesis + different forks we should have different fork hashes Could lead to interesting test case where you have a devnet with new fork, and the devnet without it (so you can replay all txs) produce block beacon apis

Hi guys, we think we've found an issue while debugging, we were supplied a genesis with a nonce of 0x01 in the address 0x0b but it seems that other clients either ignore it or it should be 0, and secondly we noticed that we can only reach consensus when we increment system account nonce (which shouldn't be done)
so yeah in order for us to pass the tests we had to : 
* change genesis spec to set 0 as nonce to 0x0b 
* increment system account nonce

excerpts.author: jochembrouwer
excerpts.content:
I agree with Felix' comment but the current state of your PR will not distinguish, since:

> If multiple forks are applied at the same block or time, the block number or timestamp is checksummed only once.

This should then be removed as well, otherwise genesis for Cancun / Shanghai will still have the same CRC. What we want is (right?):

For shanghai: `<genesis hash> <homestead block (0)> <tangerine whistle (0> ... <shanghai time (0)>`
For cancun:  `<genesis hash> <homestead block (0)> <tangerine whistle (0> ... <shanghai time (0)> <cancun time (0)>`
(all are padded to 4 bytes except ofc. genesis hash of 32 bytes).

With the rule which I think it should be deleted, this is the result:

For shanghai: `<genesis hash> <homestead block (0)>`
For cancun:  `<genesis hash> <homestead block (0)>`
(i.e. still same CRC32)
